fields.sample_size: interviews with nine key informants as stated in the text; the roles listed add up to twelve (head of the regional rural water office and three directorate officials, four chairpersons of a Local Water User Association and four of Water Point Committees), so the total is ambiguous; mixed methods with document review (the title page abstract says qualitative and quantitative, but no survey sample is reported)

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a qualitative key-informant case study in one Namibian region (nine to twelve interviewees); read in full text 2026-10-04.
pdf_note: African Studies Quarterly 21(1):28-42 (2022), full text read in Drive file S394_Salom_N_2022...pdf
notes: Checked against the full text: findings match the extraction (Water Act 54 of 1956 still in force, Water Resource Management Act 11 of 2013 not operational, no regulator, no committee elections or incentives). The stated interview count (nine) and the roles listed (twelve) do not agree in the paper.
